Definition: to babble; hence, to vociferate angrily
BiblicalUsage: Bata means to speak rashly, to babble out words without thinking. The law says a man who swears rashly with his lips is guilty when he knows it, the proverb says rash words are like the piercings of a sword while the tongue of the wise is health, and the psalm says Moses spoke unadvisedly with his lips at Meribah.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rash words are the easiest sin and the hardest to take back, because a sword-thrust of a sentence cannot be unsaid. Moses himself spoke unadvisedly once, and I hold that his failure is our warning: even the meekest man must guard his mouth.
